messages:
maria_support: Customer inbound — reported intermittent 401s and a billing spike tied to a prompt that contains sensitive customer identifiers (SSN-like string). They're worried about handing over raw prompts. Can we coordinate a sanitized repro and what exact IDs/logs we need?

dennis_dev: Thanks — can you paste the request_id(s) and approximate timestamps? We need the request_id to look up infra traces. Also we usually ask for a minimal curl that reproduces the error, with tokens/keys removed.

maria_support: Request IDs: req_2026-04-02-0451 and req_2026-04-02-0453 (timestamps 2026-04-02T04:51:12Z and 04:51:45Z). Attaching user-provided prompt but replaced obvious PII with [REDACTED] for now. They asked for us not to share raw SSN anywhere.

sam_oncall: Ok — two parts: 1) for infra we need request_id + raw server logs (we can redact PII in logs locally), 2) for reproducer we just need a curl with the same prompt structure and same model/params. Recommend pseudonymization instead of outright redaction so we can preserve tokenization/length characteristics.

sam_oncall: Example approach: replace every numeric sequence that looks like SSN with a stable token like PERSON_ID_1 so length stays similar. Keep a local mapping file that never leaves our systems. Then produce the curl using the pseudonymized prompt.

privacy-bot: Tip: run the debug-bundle collector with --scrub-mode=pseudo and --exclude-headers=authorization. That will mask PII while preserving token counts.

maria_support: Can you paste a sample curl and the sed command we should run to pseudonymize? I will send that to the customer as instructions.

dennis_dev: Sample curl (replace API_KEY and MODEL):

```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-1","input":"My customer name is JOHN DOE, SSN 123-45-6789, order id ORD-98765. Need refund."}'
```

dennis_dev: Sed example to pseudonymize SSN-like patterns and names (run locally before sharing):

```bash
# pseudonymize SSN-like sequences
sed -E 's/[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}/PERSON_ID_1/g' raw_prompt.txt \
  | sed -E 's/JOHN DOE/PERSON_NAME_1/g' > pseudonymized_prompt.txt
```

sam_oncall: And here's a short repro workflow to give the customer: 1) run above sed locally to create pseudonymized_prompt.txt; 2) replace the -d JSON input with contents of that file; 3) run debug-bundle with scrub flags and attach the bundle to this thread. Use: 

```bash
# collect bundle (do NOT include auth header)
redwood-debug collect --request-id req_2026-04-02-0451 --out bundle.tar.gz --scrub-mode=pseudo --exclude-headers authorization
```

maria_support: Legal asked for a note — never share the local mapping file. Legal: any extra checklist for support to include before we request logs from customer?

legal_sme: Short checklist: 1) Confirm customer consent to share pseudonymized prompt and debug bundle. 2) Confirm mapping file will be retained only on customer side or in our secure ticket storage if customer permits. 3) If any PHI present, escalate to compliance. 4) Ensure Authorization headers removed from any shared HTTP traces.

privacy-bot: Also recommend including a short snippet showing how token lengths preserved: run tokenizer on original (customer) prompt locally and compare counts against pseudonymized prompt to verify parity.

maria_support: I'll send the repro instructions + the sample curl + sed commands to the customer and ask for the debug-bundle output. Once they attach bundle.tar.gz we can do infra trace lookups using the request IDs. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
